Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Technische Informatik; Software-Engineering; Künstliche Intelligenz; InformationswissenschaftStellenbeschreibung:As part of the German government's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the successful Saxon competence center ScaDS.AI Dresden/Leipzig (Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence) is being expanded into a leading German AI competence center for Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For TUD Dresden University of Technology, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Center for Interdisciplinary Digital Sciences (CIDS), the Department for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (ScaDS.AI Dresden) offers, subject to the availability of resources, two project positions funded by the BMFTR asResearch Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting as soon as possible. The positions are fixed-term until March 31, 2029. The individual contract duration will be determined according to the candidate’s qualifications and the intended academic qualification goal. An extension may be possible subject to the availability of resources. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). A shorter contract term is possible by arrangement. Within the project Neuro-Symbolic AI with Logic-Memory Decomposition (Neuro-SAIL), a new class of architectures for verifiable neuro-symbolic AI is being researched using Logic-Memory Decomposition. Rule-based decisions are made by logic components, while memory modules are only used when information is incomplete or ambiguous. If no reliable decision is possible, escalation to humans occurs. The aim is to make rule-based decisions more transparent and efficient, to limit the use of neural models to necessary cases, and to reduce rule violations and unsubstantiated statements.Professional assignment: Chair of Scalable Software Architectures for Data Analytics (Prof. Dr. Michael Färber)Research areas: Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, Knowledge Graphs, and related fields (e.g., Graph Machine Learning)Tasks: - scientific research and development activities in at least one of the above-mentioned research areas- participation in national and international research projects, possibly in collaboration with industry- preparation of publications in internationally renowned journals and presentation of research findings at conferencesRequirements: - a university degree (M.Sc., M.Eng. or equivalent) and if applicable a PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Systems, Data Science, Computational Science, Mathematics, Applied Statistics, Information Science, Information Systems, Information Systems Engineering, Electronic Information Engineering, Computational Linguistics, Digital Humanities, Linguistics, or a related field- a strong interest in fundamental research in the above-mentioned fields- strong programming skills, preferably in Python, including experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow) and related tools- good written and spoken English- strong analytical and problem-solving skills- high level of motivation and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team- research experience (publications, theses, projects) in the above-mentioned research areas is a major advantageWe offer:The position comes with access to high-performance computing resources and access to training opportunities within ScaDS.AI.TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for oneResearch associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16The Department of Predictive Cognition is a newly established research unit within the Faculty of Psychology. After the completion of the new THINK research building on the former Opel site Mark 51°7, the team will move there https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/think/index.html.en. The research focus of our department is on combining neuroimaging and behavioural measurements with computational models to understand how the human brain learns and uses prior expectations during cognition. More information can be found here: https://blanklab.eu/The position is part of the Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844), an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework, which conceptualizes episodic memory as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. When we communicate with others, our perception of their speech is continuously guided by the memory of our past interactions. But how? In this CRC subproject A16 " Integration of episodic traces and semantic other-person models in a social context", we will investigate how memory traces of previously heard dialogues and the other-person model, which contains general semantic knowledge about the person, modify speech perception. This project places the generative model of scenario construction within a social context. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigate how EM traces and other-person models differentially influence the neural representation of speech and language. We are looking for an enthusiastic researcher with a Master's degree in psychology, cognitive science, or a related field and strong programming and statistical skills to carry out the proposed project.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)Start: 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-30Your tasks:- Organization and execution of experimental research work, from programming experimental setups, data acquisition, and data analysis, to the dissemination of the results- Acquisition of MRI data- Analysis and publication of MRI data- Practice of Open Science Practices- Close collaboration with PIs and ECRs from other subprojectsYour profile:- A Master of Science or an equivalent degree in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, or a related discipline- Strong programming and statistical skills- Experience in experimental approaches to study predictive processing, memory, learning, and communication- Prior experience with fMRI is an advantage- Experience and keen interest in using large language models- Strong organizational skills- A high level of spoken and written English- Highly self-motivated and eager to learn- Working independently, in a structured manner, and with a focus on results- Enjoy working as part of an interdisciplinary team of researchershttps://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA)

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Junior Research Group Crosstalk (head: Dr. Melanie Mittenbühler) at the Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry focuses on how inter-tissue communication impacts energy balance and metabolic health. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. Our group investigates how skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ and communicates with other tissues through secreted signaling molecules, particularly myokines. We aim to identify novel exercise-sensitive myokines and define their roles in sarcopenia, metabolic disease, and cancer biology.
